subject.title: fix: order ambient transcript watermarks by decimal ids

question: For message IDs without a channel-defined order, should the watermark track every observed ID at the maximum timestamp, or should OpenClaw define a deterministic total order over the strings?
rationale: A single `messageId` cannot safely represent multiple unordered messages sharing one timestamp; choosing the persistent boundary semantics affects replay correctness and potentially stored session-state compatibility.

options.title: Track IDs at the timestamp
options.body: Represent the maximum timestamp with a bounded set of observed IDs so equal-timestamp duplicates are rejected without inventing an ordering.

options.title: Define a total string order
options.body: Document and test a stable cross-channel ordering for noncanonical IDs, accepting that it may not match channel arrival order.

options.title: Restrict support to ordered IDs
options.body: Keep the current single-ID model and require affected channels to supply canonical ordered IDs or higher-resolution timestamps.

recommendation.title: Track IDs at the timestamp
recommendation.body: Represent the maximum timestamp with a bounded set of observed IDs so equal-timestamp duplicates are rejected without inventing an ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent replay-deduplication and session-runtime work makes this the strongest available routing signal for the boundary-semantics decision.
